previous_statement: For eta small enough that ||X^2-I||_{inf->inf}<1, define (X^2)^(-1/2) by the convergent binomial series and theta(X)=(I+X(X^2)^(-1/2))/2. The series commutes with X, fixes 1, and satisfies ||(X^2)^(-1/2)-I||_{inf->inf} <= K eta for a universal K; hence S=X(X^2)^(-1/2) has S^2=I, S1=1, and ||S-X||_{inf->inf} <= C eta.
new_statement: Using the validated sibling 1.1.1, write Y=X^2-I with X1=1, ||X||_{inf->inf}<=3, and ||Y||_{inf->inf}<=4 eta. For eta<=1/8 define B=(X^2)^(-1/2)=(I+Y)^(-1/2) by the convergent binomial series and set S=XB and theta(X)=(I+S)/2. Then B commutes with X, B1=1, ||B-I||_{inf->inf}<=8 eta; hence S^2=I, S1=1, and ||S-X||_{inf->inf}<=24 eta.
